items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: And he worked with Kid Orrish and Mudcarrier. And he worked with King Arthur. Mm-hmm. Dead Green, King Arthur. That's the most band that I know he worked with. Sid and Dead Green, King Arthur and Kid Orrish.

ctx.x: They make them themselves? No, no. They bought them, huh? Yeah. They bought them. Now, what do you call jazz music? How would you demonstrate jazz tempo?

That's in order of speaking about it just a while ago. Fast. Yeah. Do you know when that word began being used around here in connection with the bands, when they started calling them jazz bands? About what year? Was it before the war, after the First World War? When was it, do you know? I think it was after the First World War. I think it was after the First World War. Yeah, after the First World War. Because that, before then, it left a dish around here. Well, to change the subject again, I'd like to get back…
You and Barney? No. You haven't played together in a while.

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: King, uh, Kid Ory. At Mudkara. Where was that? On, at the National Park.

ctx.x: Might have been. Was he the cornet player?

The trumpet player, yeah. Yeah, Albert. Well, he changed musicians a lot, huh? Oh, yeah, he changed musicians a lot. Did you ever hear Oliver play? Oh, yeah, King Oliver. How did he work when you heard him? Do you remember how he was playing? Where did he work at? Mm-hmm. The time I heard King Oliver, he was playing the color dance at the Economy Hall. What? Economy Hall. Then he used to play at the National Park sometimes. He'd be on third in the South Carolina. He used to have a big park there. Was that for…
You remember if that was, I suppose that would be the album system, the same as Barney played.

items.title: Alex Bigard Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: Henry Martin was playing the drum with the, with Kid Ores and there.

ctx.x: Did you ever sit in with them? Oh, no, I wasn't, I was not playing music then.

Oh, I see. I was a kid. Oh, I didn't hear that. I know Bunk, when he saw Barney in San Francisco, that was 15 years ago, he said to Barney, you won't remember me, but I remember you. And I used to go to your uncle's house. Okay, yeah. He played violin. He told Barney all about his family more than Barney could remember, he said. That's right. And he said he remembers Barney being a little kid playing around there, but Barney wouldn't remember Bunk. I was a kid too, and I used to admire when my uncle would have…
Who did he play with him?
